text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong expressed confidence in the long-term economic prospects for the troubled Thai economy after a three-day official visit to Thailand.

- The Royal Brothers, Raj and Ashok Kumar, were charged in court with offering at least Singapore $1 million as a bribe to the general manager of HL Bank, the Singapore branch of Malaysia's Hong Leong Bank two years ago.
- Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Virawan said he would resign, ending months of speculation which has buffeted Thailand's embattled stock market.
- Singapore banks operating in Thailand as offshore lending institutions have a good chance of upgrading to full-licence branches, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said.
- Amcol Holdings shares are each backed by net tangible assets of 83 cents, say independent property valuers.
- In a surprise decision, the High Court has dismissed as unenforceable the option granted to Rafiq Jumabhoy to buy his family's entire 42 percent stake in listed Scotts Holdings Ltd.
- Ekran Bhd boss Ting Pek Khiing has scrapped the proposed rights issue of Bakun Hydroelectric Company, the operator of the planned M$15.5 billion dam in Sarawak.
- Brokerage house Kim Eng Holdings announced a solid increase in year-end earnings, as well as the intended sale of a 40 percent stake of its Hong Kong arm to its own managers.
- Keppel Land emerged the top bidder for a freehold site in Sunset Way with its offer of Singapore $77.1 million in a tender which closed on Tuesday.
